text: The Levites "bore" the ark. Isaiah says Jesus "bore" our sicknesses. Same word. Lift up His Son, and His Son lifts your load.
explanation:
After Uzzah's death, David learned that God's way was for the Levites to carry the ark on their shoulders. The Hebrew word for carry there is nasa, to lift up. It's the same word in Isaiah 53: "Surely He has borne [nasa] our griefs and carried [sabal] our sorrows"; sabal means to carry a heavy load.

While preparing this message, Joseph Prince sensed the Lord say: "If you will bear My Son, My Son will bear your sicknesses." Exalt Jesus in your home, your work and your relationships, and He carries your pains, your depression and your infirmities away. You lift Him up; He lifts your heaviest loads.

text: "God helped the Levites who bore the ark." If what you carry for Him crushes you, it isn't His yoke.
explanation:
The gold-covered ark was heavy: a load of some seventy pounds for each of the four bearers. Yet Scripture says God helped them. Jewish tradition describes it this way: once they lifted the ark, it was as if the ark carried them.

Jesus said, "My yoke is easy and My burden is light." He took the crushing load of our sins and pains so that what He gives us to carry is light. If something religious is pressing down on you, grating like a heavy yoke, it isn't from Him. Whatever He truly calls you to, He gives the grace to make it easy.

text: You might be trembling, but the mountain you're standing on never trembles.
explanation:
When God gave the law, Sinai quaked, thick darkness covered it, and even Moses said, "I am exceedingly afraid and trembling." But "you have not come to the mountain that may be touched… but you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God," the mountain of grace.

"Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, but abides forever." God is shaking everything that can be shaken, everything man boasts in. You may feel shaky, but you stand on a mountain that can't move. And Hebrews' answer to the shaking is simple: "Let us have grace."

text: "We were hoping that it was He who was going to redeem Israel." They loved what Jesus could do more than Jesus Himself.
explanation:
On the road to Emmaus, two discouraged disciples poured out their disappointment to a stranger they didn't recognise. Their hearts were set on Israel's redemption; Jesus had been a means to that end. So He didn't simply fix their hopes. "Beginning at Moses and all the Prophets, He expounded to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself."

It's easy to make Jesus a means to an end too: for the career, the healing, the family. He cares about all of those. But what warmed their hearts was seeing Him. Put Him at the centre, and everything else finds its place.

text: When God restores, it's never just back to how it was. Water becomes wine.
explanation:
God promises to rebuild David's fallen tabernacle and repair its breaches: "I will build it as in the days of old." And then come the overflowing harvests and wine on the mountains. His restorations are always greater, in quality or in quantity.

When He restores your marriage, don't expect it simply to return to what it was. What was water becomes wine. Joseph Prince says that after decades of marriage he finds himself in a new season of falling in love with his wife. Whatever has broken in your life, God's repair will surpass the original.

text: Lust and greed are the voice of a dead man. Don't keep crying to God about him as if he's alive.
explanation:
Most teaching on overcoming the flesh prescribes more discipline and more effort. But trying harder implies Jesus didn't finish the work. Scripture says, "Reckon yourselves to be dead indeed to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus." The voice that urges you to be greedy, selfish or impure belongs to your old man, and he was crucified with Christ.

If you constantly pray against him, you're treating him as alive. That's not faith. Ignore the dead man, and keep your eyes on Jesus. Holiness grows from a conscience that knows it's forgiven; as you fall in love with Him, you fall out of love with sin.

text: "You will hear of wars and rumours of wars. See that you are not troubled."
explanation:
Jesus warned of wars, earthquakes, famines and pestilences before His return. But in the same breath He said, "See that you are not troubled; for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet." The world may grow darker, but His blessings toward His people don't depend on the headlines.

And don't mistake the destroyer for God. "The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly." Pray for the nations, including their leaders; you have influence with God. Then rest. Your peace is anchored in Him.
